findings.F1: The result is unclear for a mechanical reason, not a weak effect. The main measure is on the predicted side, +0.55 % unusual move over 18 bars with t 3.74 over 2891 cases. But the cube-and-pivot transform saturates the forecast: 61 % of cases sit at -20 and the median |forecast| is 20.00, so the above-median group was empty (0 against 2891 cases) and the supporting check could not be computed.
findings.F2: Inside the cases the grading the idea claims is missing, and for the strongest situations it is reversed.
findings.F3: The situation is rarely a run. The streak length is 1 bar at the median of three of the four length quartiles and 2 bars in the top one. The cases are mostly "one 4h up-close while below the 30-day average", not an extended streak.
findings.F4: The move builds slowly rather than as a quick give-back.
findings.F5: The effect sits mostly in the early years.
findings.F6: Volume works against the brief's claim. Among the 606 cases with streaks of 2 or more bars:
findings.F7: The effect is broad but faint across coins. All six coins are positive, from +0.29 % (XMR) to +0.81 % (ETH), and only ETH reaches t ≥ 2 (t 2.49).
findings.F8: The idea's size does not cover a trade. The total move per case is +0.14 % against a 0.19 % cost (0.7 times the cost), and the book's Sharpe is -0.09. A larger move per case would be needed for any book on it to pay, whatever the holding or the sizing.

ideas.idea: A four-hour up-close made on volume rising across the streak, while the coin's price is below its average of the past 30 days, is followed by a fall relative to the coin's usual drift over the next three days; the larger the rise in volume across the streak, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorting relief rallies inside a 30-day downtrend would favour the bounces that come on swelling volume and refuse those on fading volume, where the give-back is smaller.
ideas.name: rising-volume relief rally fades
